problem: Suppose that $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events. Given that $P(A)=0.5$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.7,$ find $P(B).$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability Involving Mutually Exclusive Events
examples.problem: Suppose that $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events. Given that $P(A)=\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $P(A\cup B) = \dfrac{4}{9},$ find $P(B).$
examples.worked_solution:
If $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events, then $P(A\cap B) = 0.$ 

Therefore, by the addition law, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B) \\ P(B) & =P(A\cup B)-P(A) \\  & =\frac{4}{9}-\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{4-3}{9} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Given $P(A)=\frac{2}{7},$ $P(B)=\frac{1}{3},$ and $P(A\cup B)=\frac{10}{21},$ determine whether $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.
feedback.worked_solution:
To check if $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, we must check that $P(A\cap B)=0.$

We can calculate $P(A\cap B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{10}{21} & =\frac{2}{7}+\frac{1}{3}-P(A\cap B) \\ P(A\cap B) & =\frac{2}{7}+\frac{1}{3}-\frac{10}{21} \\  & =\frac{6+7-10}{21} \\  & =\frac{1}{7} \\  & \ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: $A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events, since $P(A\cap B)\ne 0$
